12.2
Εως πότε, Κύριε, ἐπιλήσῃ μου εἰς τέλος; ε ως πότε ἀποστρέψεις τὸ πρόσωπόν σου
ἀπ' ἐμοῦ; Τοῦ αὐτοῦ. ∆ιδάσκων, τῆς μνήμης τοῦ Θεοῦ καιρῷ τινι ἀποπεπτωκέναι
[τὴν λήθην]· (λήθην γὰρ ὁ Θεὸς ποιεῖται τῶν λανθανόν των αὐτοῦ· λανθάνει δὲ
αὐτοῦ πᾶς ὁ ἁμαρ τάνων)· ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐπεὶ ἀποστρέφει τὸ πρόσω πον αὑτοῦ ἀπὸ τῶν
αἰσχρόν τι πραττόντων ἀναξίως τῶν αὐτοῦ ὀφθαλμῶν, τουτέστι τῆς θεωρητικῆς
καὶ ἐπισκοπικῆς αὐτοῦ δυνά μεως, βιούντων μεγάλως φροντιζόντων περὶ τῆς
κρίσεως τοῦ Θεοῦ, καὶ ἀγωνιῶν ἐφ' οι ς ἑαυτῷ συνῄδει, πληττόμενός τε ὑπὸ τοῦ
συνειδότος, καὶ τὴν ψυχὴν ὑπὸ λογισμῶν ἀνιώμενος, ἐπιλέγει·
pass_a_gloss: Until when, Lord, will-you-forget me into end? until when will-you-turn the face of-you from me? Of-the same. Teaching, of-the memory of-the God at-time some to-have-fallen [the forgetfulness]; (forgetfulness for the God makes of-the ones-escaping-notice of-him; escapes-notice and of-him every the one-sinning); but also since he-turns the face of-himself from the shameful something doing unworthily of-the of-him eyes, that-is of-the contemplative and overseeing of-him power, of-ones-living greatly thinking about the judgment of-the God, and being-in-agony upon which to-himself he-knew-with, being-struck both by the conscience, and the soul by reasonings being-distressed, he-adds:
pass_b_english: “How long, Lord, will you forget me unto the end? How long will you turn your face from me?” (Psalm 12:2).

Of the same. Teaching that forgetfulness has fallen from the memory of God at a certain time (for God makes forgetfulness of those who escape his notice; and everyone who sins escapes his notice); but also since he turns his own face from those who do something shameful, unworthily of his eyes, that is of his contemplative and overseeing power, of those living who think greatly about the judgment of God, and being in agony over what he knew with himself, being struck by conscience, and the soul being distressed by reasonings, he adds:

choices.term: λήθην γὰρ ὁ Θεὸς ποιεῖται τῶν λανθανόντων αὐτοῦ
choices.english: God makes forgetfulness of those who escape his notice
choices.why: λανθάνει πᾶς ὁ ἁμαρτάνων: the sinner is out of God’s memory/face. Not ‘God has amnesia’.
rejected: God never forgets anyone who sins

anf_compare.notes: ANF lacks this Greek catena as reading English.
